clue.text: After drink quiet worker is pert

indicators.note: the quiet worker is placed after the drink, so these pieces follow it in order

parts.note: a flip is a drink of beaten egg with spirit or beer
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet
the ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone gets cheeky with a quiet employee once they have had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone cheeky and lacking proper respect.

indicators.note: the disease's name is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: brand is a fungal disease of plants, a kind of rust or smut

explanation.surface: A healthy food is said to have cut down a plant blight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims BRAND to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal husks are sold as a fibre-rich staple of health-food shops.

clue.text: Officer makes contract, fourth in hearts

parts.note: to purse the lips is to draw them together, contract them

indicators.note: the letter in fourth position of the word hearts is taken

explanation.surface: An officer signs a deal with the fourth card in a hand of hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fourth in' picks R, the fourth letter of 'hearts', added after PURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer in charge of accounts and passengers' welfare.

indicators.note: the social group holds the collection within it, as if carrying it

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
a set is a collection of matching things

explanation.surface: A club takes round a box for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts SET inside CASTE, between CAS and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cassette is a small plastic case holding the tape.

clue.text: Sock darned with wool for forest dweller

indicators.note: to sock is to hit hard, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sock mended with wool is worn by someone living in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' is the verb meaning thump, not the garment, and signals that the letters of DARNED and WOOL be rearranged; 'darned' is fodder, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives among the trees of a wood.

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the letters run upwards, so are read in reverse

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A bird's call is a cry as it flies high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when soaring' turns the whole of TI + WEEP upwards, giving PEEWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the lapwing, after its call.

parts.note: these three letters are what you get when the word all is turned the other way round

explanation.surface: Some odd letters seem to show they are good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: LLA is ALL written round the other way, read as ALL ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: All-round means competent in every respect, so good enough for any task.

indicators.note: the letters of old are scattered into a new order

parts.note: men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: An ancient stone table has old pieces strewn about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges OLD to DOL, then MEN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric tomb of upright stones topped by a flat slab, resembling a table.

parts.note: more means longer or extra, as in 'a little more'
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A tenor sings a lengthier love song.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoret is a love poem or sonnet, from the French for little love.

clue.text: American's dropped out of country trip

indicators.note: the American abbreviation is removed from the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a country in Europe
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American has quit a trip around a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped out of' takes A from SPAIN, leaving SPIN; the printed answer SPAN cannot come from this wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure trip, as in going for a spin in the car.

parts.note: not a jetty but the landing phase of a space mission, ending in the sea

explanation.surface: It looks like a question about a jetty for boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's return to Earth by coming down in the ocean is the final stage of its mission.

clue.text: German at end of bar, a Frankfurter, possibly

indicators.note: the German abbreviation is placed after the word for bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar or forbid

explanation.surface: A German sits at the end of the bar, a man from Frankfurt perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frankfurter' looks like a person from Frankfurt; it is the sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for a sausage, and a frankfurter is one kind.

clue.text: Effect of ghost, mainly — else, of shivering?

definitions.text: Effect of ghost, mainly — else, of shivering?

indicators.note: the letters shiver and shake themselves into a new arrangement
only most of the word is used, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A ghost mostly makes you shiver, if nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts GHOST to GHOS; 'shivering' rearranges GHOS + ELSE + OF; the whole clue is also the definition, since a ghost gives you the shivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumpy skin raised by fear or cold, which a ghost might bring on.

indicators.note: the letters are organised, arranged into a fresh order

parts.note: the word centre, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A recess at the community centre has been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges AT CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is the interval between two acts of a play.

indicators.note: the subject goes round the outside of the royal letter

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A subject stands apart from the royal line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TOPIC round R.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude.

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is batting is said to be in
a score is a scratched line, like a crease or fold

explanation.surface: A cricketer while batting adds runs to the total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like the runs total; it is a scored line. 'Batting' gives IN, and in cricket the crease is also the line where the batter stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Minor decoration given to the French officer

parts.note: a bead is a small ornament
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An officer is awarded a small medal by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish or church official who keeps order.

indicators.note: the word for look is placed inside the rearranged letters
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Shellfish are seen in rock pools and stony places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges PLACES to ESCAP; 'in' puts LO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop is a scallop, a bivalve mollusc.

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for Sunday or sun

indicators.note: the word for soft is wrapped round the compass point

parts.note: mild means soft or gentle
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The sun shone gently in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts MILD round E, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to grin broadly.

clue.text: Trendy word around company for calling system

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: the word goes round the company abbreviation

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A fashionable word is spreading round the firm about the phone system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts TERM round CO, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-way internal phone or speaker system in a building.

definitions.meaning: ill feeling or antagonism between rivals
hype is slang for a hypodermic, a syringe with a sharp point

explanation.definitionFit: Needle means rivalry or hostility, and is also the sharp hollow spike of a hypodermic syringe.

indicators.note: a different form of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Honesty is a kind of creditworthiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward and frank, without evasion.

indicators.note: the editor is wrapped up inside the word for leader

parts.note: Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title
ED is the abbreviation for editor, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Suppose the editor is involved with the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts ED inside DUCE, Italian for leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer or conclude something from evidence.

clue.text: Loaded, but with a spring in one's step?

definitions.text: with a spring in one's step?
definitions.meaning: read as shoes with good heels giving a bounce to the walk

explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled means wealthy, and taken literally it describes shoes with fine heels.

definitions.meaning: a colour that is not deep is light or faint

explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a pointed stake in a fence, and as an adjective it means light in colour.

indicators.note: the word for spy lacks its final letter, so is unfinished

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: The spy has left his mission incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention or scheme.

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: A book weathers scathing reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasts are fierce verbal attacks or rebukes.

clue.text: He expects to be take at his word

definitions.text: He expects to be take at his word

parts.words: He expects to be take at his word
parts.note: one who dictates, whose spoken word is law and is written down as said

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'take' stands for 'taken'. Words a dictator says are obeyed, and dictated words are taken down as spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler whose orders must be obeyed, and also one who dictates letters.
